# three-fiber-component-shape-planner (reference summary)

## Purpose
Plan the React Three Fiber component shape (props, refs, Suspense, useGLTF cache, animation hooks) before delivering a GLB to a web team.

Translate a planned GLB delivery into the exact public surface a React Three Fiber component should expose, so the web engineer's contract is locked before code is written.

## Metadata & truth boundary
- **Canonical skill:** `skills/three-fiber-component-shape-planner/SKILL.md`
- **Contract:** `skills/three-fiber-component-shape-planner/contract.json` (`v1.0.0`)
- **Category / role:** `evidence-and-handoff` / `r3f-component-contract-architect`
- **Capability tier:** `L0`
- **Truth-state policy:** Runtime status defaults to `Not Run`; Artifact status defaults to `Not Produced`; mutation rule is `downgrade_only` (never upgrade without verified evidence).

## When to use
- the GLB will ship to a web app using React Three Fiber
- before the web team writes the component
- when "I'll just import the GLB" needs more rigor (multiple clips, prop overrides, lazy loading)

## Trigger cues
- "how should the React component look"
- "what props should I expose"
- "ref shape for the model"
- "we use react-three-fiber"

## When not to use
- consumers using vanilla Three.js (different API) → delegate to `glb-web-handoff` (`references/skills/glb-web-handoff.md`; different API)
- consumers using Babylon / model-viewer (different stack) → delegate to `glb-animation-handoff` (`references/skills/glb-animation-handoff.md`; different stack)
- the GLB is rendered server-side (e.g. AR pre-render); no React component needed → delegate to `non-blender-user-response-writer` (`references/skills/non-blender-user-response-writer.md`; Delegates out-of-scope requests to non-blender-user-response-writer)

## Inputs & output/evidence contract
### Required inputs
- `glb_delivery_contract` (`object`): Locked GLB node hierarchy, material slots, and compression spec from glb-web-handoff
- `r3f_version_and_use_case` (`object`): Target @react-three/fiber major version (8 vs 9) and interactive component use case

### Optional inputs
- `animation_clip_contract` (`object`): Optional clip names, triggers, and crossfade rules from glb-animation-handoff

### Primary outputs
- `r3f_component_props_and_ref_spec`
- `suspense_caching_and_dispose_contract`
- `consumer_call_site_usage_outline`

## Quick-start procedure
1. enumerate the props the consumer needs (color, animation name, scale, onLoaded)
2. decide ref shape (forwardRef, imperative methods)
3. decide Suspense boundary location
4. decide useGLTF caching + cleanup strategy
5. decide animation hook contract (auto-play, manual control)

## Handoff notes
- **[upstream_reference]** Animation contract → `glb-animation-handoff` (`references/skills/glb-animation-handoff.md`)
- **[upstream_reference]** Performance budget ceilings → `glb-mobile-performance-budget` (`references/skills/glb-mobile-performance-budget.md`)
- **[upstream_reference]** Color and material checks (color-management-decision) → `color-management-decision` (`references/skills/color-management-decision.md`)
- **[upstream_reference]** Color and material checks (material-quality-checker) → `material-quality-checker` (`references/skills/material-quality-checker.md`)
- **[upstream_reference]** Web delivery packaging → `glb-web-handoff` (`references/skills/glb-web-handoff.md`)
- **[progression]** Final user-facing response → `non-blender-user-response-writer` (`references/skills/non-blender-user-response-writer.md`)

## Safety boundaries & non-goals
- **Runtime boundary:** This skill produces **planning specs only**. It does not generate component code, run a web app, or claim that the resulting component will perform correctly without measured load tests. Web-side implementation is owned by the consumer team.
- Generate React or Three.js component implementation code.
- Run web apps or execute React Three Fiber at runtime.
- Claim or verify web runtime performance.
- Upgrade truth states (web runtime belongs to the consumer team, not BlendOps).
- Own animation contracts, performance budgets, color/material validation, or web delivery packaging.
